headline: Woodside exits Bonaparte CCS as INPEX takes full control and moves the project into FEED
summary: INPEX agreed to acquire Woodside's 21% stake in the INPEX-led Bonaparte CCS JV (~260 km offshore Darwin), lifting INPEX to 74% via a new entity INPEX Bonaparte CCS Pty Ltd (subject to regulatory approval); the JV has commenced FEED, targeting first CO2 injection in the early 2030s with Ichthys LNG as anchor customer.
co2crc_note: Australia's flagship offshore CCS project consolidates under a single operator and enters FEED — a major domestic milestone directly relevant to CO2CRC's home-market CCS pipeline and Darwin/Ichthys emissions abatement.
extractor_note: Stake-transfer + FEED-entry item; no money figure stated. Capacity (cited ~8-10 Mtpa / 443 Mt over 35 yrs elsewhere) not restated in this article, left null to avoid additive confusion.

headline: PETRONAS, TotalEnergies and Mitsui sign JV agreement to develop Southern CCS Hub storage area off Peninsular Malaysia
summary: The trio signed a JV agreement to form a company developing a CO2 storage area offshore Peninsular Malaysia (Malaysia's Southern CCS Hub); phase one targets a depleted gas field with up to 5 Mtpa injection capacity and first injection as early as 2031, building on their 2023 Development Agreement and 2025 Key Principles Agreement. The hub is designed for domestic and cross-border CO2.
co2crc_note: A regional transboundary CCS hub taking cross-border CO2 — a direct comparator and potential competitor/partner to Australia's own cross-border storage ambitions (Bonaparte, Bayu-Undan); Mitsui's involvement signals Japanese demand for APAC storage.
extractor_note: JV formation ahead of FID; no money figure stated. 5 Mtpa is phase-one injection-capacity target.

headline: Skytree, Galetech and Mwahera to add direct air capture to Kenya's Mwangea e-Fuels Project
summary: The partners signed an agreement to integrate Skytree's DAC technology into the Mwangea e-Fuels Project in Kenya, combining captured CO2 with green hydrogen for carbon-neutral e-fuels; begins with an initial deployment phase and could scale to tens of kilotonnes of CO2 a year, with Skytree claiming sub-US$100/t costs.
co2crc_note: A rare African DAC-to-e-fuels catch; limited direct Australian relevance but useful signal on DAC cost claims and power-to-X demand for captured CO2.
extractor_note: Radar item — signing dated 21 Oct, just outside the Mon 23-26 window. Capacity 'tens of kilotonnes' is vague/aspirational; left null.
